clue.text: Second mating so wrong for him?

definitions.text: Second mating so wrong for him?

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of their proper order and need setting right

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who takes only one partner would think a second liaison is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: MO plus a rearrangement of MATING SO gives MONOGAMIST, the sort of man to whom a second partner is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone faithful to a single spouse regards taking another partner as improper, so the whole question describes him.

clue.text: They might make maiden freeze

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
to ice something is to freeze it

explanation.surface: Small creatures that would make a young woman stand rigid with fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it is the cartoon picture of a girl frozen by rodents, and M beside ICE spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rodents are the traditional cause of a startled scream and paralysed terror in cartoons and comic stories.

clue.text: He sailed when all the mates were aboard

definitions.text: He sailed when all the mates were aboard

parts.words: He sailed when all the mates were aboard
parts.note: surface reading: a captain who left port once his ship's officers had joined; setter's reading: mates are breeding pairs of animals, two of every kind, loaded onto a vessel before the Flood

explanation.walkthrough: Mates suggests ship's officers, but here it means animal partners, which points to the biblical ark builder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch took every creature aboard in pairs before sailing through the Flood.

clue.text: Valuable coat recovered using information about previous swindle

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
previous in the sense of former
to fleece someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A precious fur coat was got back by police acting on a tip-off about an earlier con.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information. The coat is the ram's fleece Jason and the Argonauts brought back from Colchis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the golden ram's hide was a prized object retrieved by Jason, so it is a valuable coat recovered.

clue.text: Way pronouncement is made in the House

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so we go by how the word sounds

parts.note: a way of doing something is a manner

explanation.surface: Suggests a formal declaration delivered in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: The House looks like Parliament, but it is a stately home; a manor house is often just called the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country house with its lands, the principal house of an estate.

clue.text: Writer revealing extremes of Secret Service, almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Secret
evensong is the evening service of the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A spy author exposing the shadowy fringes of the Secret Service, or nearly so.
explanation.walkthrough: Secret Service looks like one unit, but the words work separately: the ends of Secret, then the church service EVENSONG without its G, give STEVENSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson, the Scottish novelist of Treasure Island and Kidnapped, is a famous author.

clue.text: Mob was audibly triumphant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gang or group of people
second meaning: the old past tense of crow, to boast loudly

explanation.surface: A crowd made a lot of noise celebrating a win.
explanation.walkthrough: As in the cock crew, the verb crow once had this as its past tense; crowing is loud gloating.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a gang or team, and is also the archaic past tense of the verb meaning to exult loudly.

clue.text: People taking paper to get place in university

definitions.meaning: first meaning: all those who buy a newspaper
second meaning: the post of a reader, a senior lecturer

explanation.surface: Students sitting an exam paper to win a university place.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a reader ranks just below a professor, and the post is named after the role.
explanation.definitionFit: The audience of a publication, and the academic position of a reader at a British university.

clue.text: Allowing alcohol to Afghan type who discourages spirits

parts.note: a wet area is one where alcohol is permitted, the opposite of dry
an afghan is a knitted or crocheted blanket

explanation.surface: Offering a drink to a man from Afghanistan who disapproves of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirits looks like alcohol, continuing the drinking theme, but it means high spirits, a good mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy is someone who damps down others' enthusiasm, so he dampens high spirits.

clue.text: British professor in US space programme

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Arthur Conan Doyle's Professor of The Lost World
second meaning: the NASA shuttle lost in 1986

explanation.surface: An academic from Britain working for NASA.
explanation.walkthrough: Conan Doyle's irascible scientist leads The Lost World expedition; the same name belonged to a NASA space shuttle.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a famous fictional British scientist and the name of an American orbiter in the shuttle fleet.

clue.text: Reported obstacle in way of constitutional progress

indicators.note: something reported is spoken aloud by someone, so the sound matters

parts.note: a gate is a barrier blocking a path

explanation.surface: Sounds like a political report on a hurdle to constitutional reform.
explanation.walkthrough: Constitutional suggests politics, but here it is a health-giving walk, and the manner of walking is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a daily stroll, and the way one moves along on foot is one's walking style.

clue.text: Befuddled by ales, rather, as this will show

definitions.text: Befuddled by ales, rather, as this will show

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so the letters are muddled up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver drunk on beer will be found out by a roadside test.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: this device reveals that someone is befuddled by ale.
explanation.definitionFit: The police roadside device measures alcohol on the breath, so it shows whether a driver is drunk.

clue.text: Author of allegorical novel set in no man's land

definitions.text: Author of allegorical novel set in no man's land

parts.words: Author of allegorical novel set in no man's land
parts.note: surface reading: a war novel set between the trenches; setter's reading: a farm where the animals have driven out the human owner, so no man rules it

explanation.walkthrough: No man's land suggests the First World War, but it means a land with no man in charge: Animal Farm, after the animals expel Mr Jones.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of Animal Farm, a fable in which farm beasts overthrow their human master and run the place themselves.

clue.text: One who makes the running, securing end of strife

definitions.text: One who makes the running, securing end of strife

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a pacemaker sets the speed in a race

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of strife

explanation.surface: A race leader who also brings a quarrel to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: one who makes things happen by bringing strife to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mediator who settles a dispute brings hostilities to a close and restores harmony.

clue.text: Press one's suit and straighten out formal attire

parts.note: to court is to woo, pressing a suit for someone's hand
to dress ranks is to line soldiers up straight

explanation.surface: Ironing a suit and tidying up one's formal clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Press and suit look like ironing clothes, but to press one's suit is to woo; dress is the drill command for straightening a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The prescribed clothing worn for presentation at a royal court is ceremonial formal wear.

clue.text: Is event of special sporting interest for some schoolboys?

definitions.text: Is event of special sporting interest for some schoolboys?

indicators.note: special suggests treated in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether some fixture is of particular interest to pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a handball court game played at one famous English public school, which interests only some boys.
explanation.definitionFit: A version of the handball game fives, played at a celebrated boarding school near Windsor, is a sport for a few schoolboys.

clue.text: Italian gentleman played card designed to secure two hearts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona, a stage role

definitions.text: card designed to secure two hearts
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a romantic card sent on 14 February

explanation.surface: An Italian man played a card in a game to win two hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts and card suggest a card game; the two hearts are lovers, and the gentleman is a character from The Two Gentlemen of Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two title characters in a Shakespeare comedy, and the greeting card sent to a sweetheart in February.

clue.text: Burglar's only crime can be detected therein

indicators.note: detected therein says the thing is found inside the preceding words

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A detective remark that a burglar committed just one offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles burglAR'S ONly; the crime is setting fire to property.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to a building is a serious criminal offence.

clue.text: Scientist, one involved in medical success

indicators.note: something involved in another is taken inside it

parts.note: a successful treatment heals
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A researcher played a part in a medical breakthrough.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie and Pierre, the physicists who discovered radium and polonium, share this surname as famous scientists.

clue.text: One, possibly, could be let in, much altered

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone might be allowed in after being much changed.
explanation.walkthrough: One looks like a person; it is the time of day, one o'clock, a typical midday meal hour.
explanation.definitionFit: One o'clock is an example of the midday meal hour, hence the possibly.

clue.text: Drug and pill used by gymnast

definitions.note: the definition describes rather than names the heavy exercise ball

parts.note: a drug is a medicine
pill is slang for a ball

explanation.surface: Suggests an athlete taking performance-enhancing tablets.
explanation.walkthrough: Pill is old slang for a ball, as in a tennis or golf ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy weighted sphere thrown and caught for strength training is equipment found in a gym.

clue.text: Past leader of Romantics, one with no end of verse in him

definitions.text: Past leader of Romantics, one with no end of verse in him

indicators.note: with no end means the tail is cut off

parts.note: past, as in going past or by

indicators.note: the leader of a group is at its front, so we take its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Romantics
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former head of the Romantic movement, full of endless poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the poet too: a leading Romantic with no end of verse in him. Only the opening words supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron was a leading English Romantic poet, prolific author of Don Juan and Childe Harold.

clue.text: King in ecstasy? That's funny

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: ecstasy is great happiness
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch in rapture strikes someone as amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Joky means jokey, given to jesting or meant to amuse, so it fits funny.

clue.text: Deliver cards in Kentish Town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hand out cards to players
second meaning: a seaside town in Kent, south-east England

explanation.surface: Posting greeting cards in a London district called Kentish Town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a real district of London, which disguises the second definition: a town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute playing cards round the table, and the name of a coastal town in the county of Kent.

clue.text: Experienced? Doesn't sound it

definitions.meaning: surface reading: someone with plenty of practice
setter's reading: the past tense of know is pronounced like a word meaning fresh or green, the opposite of seasoned

explanation.walkthrough: Experienced here is a past-tense verb, had knowledge of; the word for it, with its silent first letter, is said like the word for novice-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Had knowledge of, or underwent, is the past tense of know, which matches experienced as a verb.

clue.text: I caught composer smashing instrument — look into it

indicators.note: smashing breaks something into pieces, which are then reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to catching a composer breaking an instrument and asks for an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: Composer looks like it needs a name such as Bach; it is used letter for letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical device that a scientist peers into to magnify tiny things is an instrument you look into.

clue.text: This wine was revolting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pink wine, written with an accent

explanation.surface: A complaint that a wine tasted dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting looks like disgusting, but it means rebelling; the people rose against their rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink wine is rosé, and the past tense of rise, as in rising up against authority, is spelt the same.

clue.text: Mint a coin like a sovereign

parts.note: a penny is a coin
a sovereign is a monarch, so kingly

explanation.surface: Producing a coin as good as a gold sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: Mint and sovereign suggest coinage (a sovereign is a British gold coin), but mint is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a small aromatic plant of the mint family, once used in folk medicine.
